objective: Add a pricing page with three plans and a Stripe checkout button

factors.name: Unexposed
factors.why: The pricing page is public and posts to /api/checkout, which is reachable without a session.

factors.name: Low severity
factors.why: One medium advisory in the date library; nothing high or critical touches the changed files.

factors.name: Patched
factors.why: Every library with a recent advisory is on a fixed version except std/http, one patch behind.

items.text: Render the three plans from plans.json on /pricing
POST /api/checkout creates a Stripe session for the chosen plan

factors.name: Unexposed
factors.why: Public endpoint that spends a Stripe API call per request.

factors.name: Low severity
factors.why: The redirect target is fixed, not taken from the query.

factors.name: Impact
factors.why: The worst open finding is a missing rate limit on checkout: cost, not data.

factors.name: Likelihood
factors.why: Abusing it needs a script and gains the attacker nothing.

factors.name: Share of the run
factors.why: One of the 14 changed lines carries the open finding.

exploits.summary: A crafted Range header makes serveDir read past the end of a file and return a 500.
parseISO accepts a very long fraction and spends seconds on it.
Webhook signature errors leak the expected timestamp tolerance in the message.

findings.title: Checkout has no rate limit
findings.fix: Limit POST /api/checkout to 10 a minute per address.

findings.title: Plan price trusted from the request body
findings.fix: Look the price up from plans.json by plan id instead of reading it from the body.

findings.title: Stripe key read at import time
findings.fix: Read STRIPE_KEY on first use so a missing key fails the request, not the server.

notes: Exploits from the last 7 days: OSV and the GitHub advisory database.
Muse Code reviewed the 14 changed lines in 3 files.
